title: Chapter 3: The Spouter-Inn — Action Spine
adaptation_principle: Track only the narrator’s concrete moves: entering, asking for a bed, refusing and improvising, confronting the landlord and understanding the 'head,' accepting the room, witnessing the harpooneer’s rites, the bed-springing confrontation, and the final acceptance that closes the chapter’s turn.

Ishmael (narrator).visual_description: Young adult sailor, average build, clean-shaven, dark hair, wearing a worn dark monkey jacket over a plain shirt, rough trousers, and sea-scuffed boots; carries himself wary but curious.

Peter Coffin (landlord).visual_description: Lean New Englander, late middle-age, angular face with a wry grin, hair tied back or under a cap; simple waistcoat and rolled-up shirtsleeves; practical hands that plane wood or whittle.

Queequeg (harpooneer).role: South Seas harpooneer and Ishmael’s future bedfellow
Queequeg (harpooneer).visual_description: Tall, powerfully built; skin with a purplish-yellow cast; face, torso, and limbs tattooed in dark square patterns; mostly bald with a small scalp-knot; wears a heavy grego/wrapall and a shaggy poncho-like cloak with quill-like tags when arriving; carries a tomahawk-shaped pipe, a seaman’s bag, a preserved head in trade, and a small polished wooden idol.

grego (heavy sailor's coat).visual_description: Bulky, dark wrapall coat with deep pockets, sea-worn.
grego (heavy sailor's coat).avoid_confusion: Not a cape; a heavy overcoat.

harpoon by bed.avoid_confusion: Keep as background prop; not used as weapon in scene.

action_oriented_synopsis: I entered the Spouter-Inn and, after close study, made out the smoke-dark painting as a ship in a gale with a whale about to impale himself upon her masts. I asked the landlord for a bed and, told the house was full, conditionally agreed to share a harpooneer’s blanket. I then changed my mind about sharing, resolved to try the bench, and found my makeshift bed foiled by knots and bitter draughts. Irritated by talk of “selling his head,” I demanded the truth and learned the harpooneer had been peddling embalmed New Zealand heads. Accepting I would not see him that night, I let the landlord lead me to the prodigious bed and looked over the harpooneer’s gear. Half-dozing, I watched the harpooneer enter, reveal his tattooed body, set up a little wooden idol, burn shavings and biscuit, and pray in strange gutturals. Tomahawk-pipe in mouth, he sprang into bed with me, I cried out, and the landlord rushed in to assure me Queequeg meant no harm. I decided better sleep with a sober cannibal than a drunken Christian, had him stash the tomahawk-pipe, turned in again, and slept soundly.

visual_safety_notes: Depict the preserved head as a small, desiccated artifact without gore or explicit anatomical detail.
Portray Queequeg’s tattoos and complexion respectfully; avoid caricature or exoticizing facial expressions.
Do not literalize metaphors (devils, angels, chaos) as visible beings or scenes.
Keep all signs, labels, clocks, and papers free of readable text.
Show the tomahawk-pipe as a pipe with a hatchet-shaped head, not as an actively wielded axe.
Fire and candle flames should be modest and controlled; do not depict spreading fire.

findings.finding: The phrase “selling his head” appears without prior setup, so the reader lacks the antecedent for the landlord’s baffling claim.
findings.repair_strategy: Add a brief setup in the preceding frame noting the landlord’s chuckling yarn about the harpooneer being out ‘selling his head,’ so Frame 4’s clarification pays off.

findings.finding: Frame 6 begins with the narrator dozing and witnessing the harpooneer’s entry, but Frame 5 doesn’t state that the narrator actually turned in.
findings.repair_strategy: Append a short clause to Frame 5 indicating the narrator turned in after inspecting the room, bridging into the doze in Frame 6.

findings.finding: The proper name “Queequeg” appears for the first time without identification.
findings.repair_strategy: Introduce the name in Frame 7 as an appositive—“the harpooneer, Queequeg”—to ground who is being named.
